при.gloss: in the presence of, in front of; at, under

meanings.en: in the presence of, in front of (a person)
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in the presence of, in front of; at, under', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет, Катя, давай спокойно с тобой поговорим.
examples.trans: Hello, Katya, let us talk calmly with you.

examples.text: Я всё понял, сейчас быстро принесу.
examples.trans: I understood everything, I will bring it quickly now.

examples.text: Сейчас всё быстро принесу.
examples.trans: I will bring everything quickly now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'first', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Деньги потом доложу при первой необходимости.
examples.trans: I will add the money later if needed.

examples.text: Это мой первый день.
examples.trans: This is my first day.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'обходимость'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'necessity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Деньги потом доложу при первой необходимости.
examples.trans: I will add the money later if needed.

examples.text: В этом нет необходимости.
examples.trans: There is no need for that.

examples.text: В этом нет никакой необходимости.
examples.trans: There is no need for that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну как тебе такой отличный план?
examples.trans: Well, how do you like such a great plan?

examples.text: Айнура, я вам квартиру не сдам.
examples.trans: Ainura, I will not rent the apartment to you.

examples.text: Что вы, я к сыну пришёл.
examples.trans: Not at all, I came to see my son.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что всё это тогда значит?
examples.trans: And what does all of this mean then?

examples.text: Что именно я ей сейчас скажу?
examples.trans: What exactly will I say to her now?

examples.text: Я скажу, что уезжаю отсюда навсегда.
examples.trans: I will say that I am leaving here forever.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'gentlemen' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну что, господа, теперь открываем карты?
examples.trans: Well then, gentlemen, do we show our cards now?

examples.text: Господа, прошу прощения.
examples.trans: Gentlemen, I apologise.

examples.text: Это господин Петров.
examples.trans: This is Mr Petrov.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь у нас точно всё кончено.
examples.trans: Now everything is definitely over between us.

examples.text: А теперь быстро уходите все отсюда.
examples.trans: And now everyone get out of here quickly.

examples.text: У Кости теперь хорошая комната освобождается.
examples.trans: A nice room is freeing up at Kostya's place now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открыть'.

examples.text: Давайте уже быстро открывать наши карты.
examples.trans: Let us quickly show our cards already.

examples.text: Ну что, господа, теперь открываем карты?
examples.trans: Well then, gentlemen, do we show our cards now?

examples.text: Идите и открывайте скорее свой сейф.
examples.trans: Go and open your safe quickly.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'cards' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Костя, я в поездах играл в карты.
examples.trans: Kostya, I played cards on trains.

examples.text: Я играл в карты.
examples.trans: I played cards.

examples.text: Я ведь просто любил играть в карты.
examples.trans: I simply loved playing cards.
